detail.body:
I'd like to implement this, and suggest a first slice without the `compress` option: `serveStaticDir(event, { dir, base, fallthrough })` exported from `h3/node`, built on the existing `serveStatic` callbacks the way [Nitro's dev wrapper](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/571aade68390676eb0e0604975119ae759804c2c/src/dev/app.ts#L200-L256) does.

Method checks, HEAD, cache validation, MIME types and index lookup would stay in `serveStatic`; the adapter only maps the id under `base` to a file in `dir` (rejecting paths outside the root after resolving symlinks), stats it and streams it. `node:fs` imports stay out of the non-Node entries.

Tests would serve from a temporary directory: root and prefixed mounts, GET/HEAD/other methods, missing files and `fallthrough`, index and cache behavior, encoded names and out-of-root paths.

Dynamic gzip/brotli would be a separate follow-up, since it adds negotiation and caching questions of its own. Would you take the uncompressed version first, or do you want compression in the same PR?

Prepared by an automated contribution pipeline that I build and operate (https://github.com/clean99/software-factory).

threadSnapshot.title: feat(node): `serveStatic` helper for a local directory
threadSnapshot.body:
Nitro's dev server has its own wrapper around `serveStatic` for serving a local directory. It maps the id to a path under the dir (with a traversal guard), uses `stat` for meta and mime type, streams the file, and can optionally gzip or brotli compress based on `accept-encoding`. Since this is generic, it could live in `h3/node` as something like `serveStaticDir(event, { dir, base, fallthrough, compress })`. That would also give users a working answer to #1578.

Current code: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/0b59022ebbf4e61259ef2bb9896633f91d396bba/src/dev/app.ts#L192-L248

threadSnapshot.title: fix(cache): expose Promise return type for withCacheIsolation wrapper
threadSnapshot.body:
Resolves #1670

withCacheIsolation wraps an event handler inside an sync function (_handlerWithCacheIsolation), so the returned wrapper always yields a Promise. However, its signature was typed as T, which preserved synchronous return types from the original handler.

As a result, calling the wrapped handler synchronously allowed accessing properties on the expected return type (e.g., esult.status or esult.headers) that evaluated to undefined or threw runtime errors because the value was a Promise.

Typing the return value as ((event: H3Event) => Promise<Awaited<ReturnType<T>>>) & T ensures the returned function signature accurately reflects the Promise result while retaining any copied properties from the wrapped handler.

threadSnapshot.title: fix(handler): don't share pending load across lazy handler requests
threadSnapshot.body:
Fixes #1661

`defineLazyEventHandler` cached the first request's pending load promise and handed it to every later request. On Cloudflare Workers a promise can only settle in the request that created it, so if that first request is cancelled mid-load, the promise never settles and every later request to the route fails until the isolate is recycled. The same sharing also meant a rejected load was cached forever.

I changed it to cache only the resolved handler, as suggested in the issue. Until a handler has resolved, each request runs its own `loader()`. For `import()` loaders this is cheap since the module registry still evaluates the module once.

One behavior change: a loader that rejects is now retried on the next request instead of replaying the cached rejection.

Testing: added a regression test (first load never settles, second rejects, third succeeds). Before the fix it times out; after, `vitest run test/handler.test.ts test/lazy.test.ts` gives 40/40 passing. oxlint, oxfmt --check and tsc are clean.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed lazy-loaded handlers becoming unavailable after a load fails or remains pending. Subsequent requests can retry loading, and successful loads continue to serve later requests.
  * Improved recovery when a handler load returns an invalid result; the request receives an error instead of leaving the handler stuck in a failed state.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
